methodological_rigor.justification: The study uses five ALL cell lines (three T-ALL, two B-ALL) with a well-designed combination of trypan blue viability, triple flow cytometry staining (MDC/Annexin V/PI) to simultaneously monitor autophagy and cell death, GR antagonism with Ru486, and systematic pharmacological modulation with RAP, SP-1, TAM, and CQ. Strengths include simultaneous readouts and inclusion of both resistant and sensitive lines. Limitations include reliance on cell lines only (no primary patient samples or in vivo validation), use of MDC which is an indirect autophagy marker (LC3 flux only assessed in Jurkat), and limited mechanistic confirmation (no GR knockdown as authors acknowledge). Statistics are appropriate with ANOVA and correct post hoc tests, n greater than or equal to 3 replicates, but effect sizes and confidence intervals are not reported for most comparisons.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is entirely in vitro preclinical work on immortalized cell lines; there is no patient data, primary sample, or animal model. Findings regarding TAM-induced autophagy and DEX sensitization are mechanistically interesting and may inform future combination trials in GC-resistant ALL, but the translational path is speculative without in vivo or primary-cell validation. Oxford LoE 5 (basic science) applies.

reporting_quality.justification: As a pure cell culture study ARRIVE does not strictly apply, but reporting of experimental setup is reasonably detailed: cell line identity with ATCC catalog numbers, reagent catalog numbers, stock preparations, passage limits, gating strategy described, and n greater than or equal to 3 replicates specified. Missing elements include explicit STAR Methods-style mycoplasma/STR authentication statements, no pre-registered analysis, no data or code availability repository, and figures/supplementary files are referenced but not accompanied by a sharing statement. Data availability is weak.

novelty_literature.justification: The dual-readout flow cytometry approach for simultaneous autophagy and cell death monitoring across a panel of GC-sensitive and -resistant ALL lines, with systematic testing of four autophagy modulators, is a useful methodological extension. The concept that TAM-induced autophagy sensitizes leukemic cells to DEX was previously reported by the same group in Jurkat cells (ref 29), so the present work extends rather than establishes a new finding. Incremental but meaningful contribution.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly written with logical flow from confirmation of sensitivity profiles, GR dependence, autophagy kinetics, to pharmacological modulation. Figures are systematically referenced and results are interpreted cautiously with appropriate acknowledgment of uncertainty (e.g., distinguishing ADCD, AMCD, AACD). Some repetition between Results and Discussion; a few figure panel callouts (Figure S2/S3) interrupt flow.

key_strengths: Simultaneous triple-stain flow cytometry (MDC/Annexin V/PI) enabling temporal dissection of autophagy and cell death in the same experiment
Panel of 5 ALL cell lines spanning GC-sensitive and -resistant phenotypes plus both T- and B-ALL lineages
Systematic testing of four autophagy modulators (RAP, TAM, SP-1, CQ) with dose-response optimization
Thoughtful discussion of ADCD/AMCD/AACD distinctions and acknowledgment of GR knockdown limitation
key_concerns: Findings limited to cell lines; no primary patient blasts, xenograft, or in vivo validation
MDC is an indirect autophagy marker; LC3-mCherry-GFP flux was only used in Jurkat cells
TAM-induced DEX sensitization in Jurkat was previously published by the same group (ref 29), limiting novelty
No data or code availability statement; effect sizes/CIs not systematically reported
GR knockdown not performed despite being acknowledged as necessary to confirm GR-independent RS4;11 mechanism
chief_reviewer.rationale: A methodologically competent preclinical cell-line study extending the authors' prior Jurkat work across additional ALL lines; novelty is modest and translational relevance is speculative, placing it in Tier 3 with minor revisions.
